title: Polyploidy influences muscle fatty acid profile and lipidomic signatures in two‐year‐old, female rainbow trout, Oncorhynchus mykiss
content:
Abstract

The proportion of rainbow trout in the consumption market in China has gradually increased, whether it is diploid or triploid. Lipids as important chemical components are closely related to the flavor and quality of rainbow trout. As the gonads are basically not developed in triploid rainbow trout, all the energy required for gonadal development can be used for body growth. Experiments have shown significant differences in fatty acid content between diploid and triploid. However, the lipidomic fingerprints of different ploidy of rainbow trout were limited. Ultraperformance liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS)-based untargeted lipidomics were done between diploid and triploid rainbow trout to reveal lipid profiles and lipid metabolism differences. According to the analysis of the results, 693 lipid molecules are classified into 5 major classes and 29 subclasses in the lipid profile of rainbow trout; 221 lipid metabolites were found with statistically significant differences, including 90 glycerol ester (GL), 96 glycerophospholipid (GP), etc. Compared to diploids, 153 lipids were downregulated and 68 were upregulated in triploid, that is consistent with the results of fatty acids contents. Among the different metabolites, phosphatidylcholine (PC) and lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC) are mainly participated in the conversion reaction in GP metabolism, which is the key metabolic pathway. The content of linoleic acid (LA) is higher in triploid rainbow trout than that in the diploid, which may be related to glycerolipid metabolism. The results provide theoretical guidance for differentiating diploid and triploid lipid metabolites composition and metabolic pathways, which is a theoretical explanation for lipid metabolism differences between diploid and triploid.
